---
title: "One day, data tools – the housing-audit case"
subtitle: "Four parts of ninety minutes, with a facilitator"
---
This is the one-day course on the housing-audit case with the tools of data science in the foreground: R, the IDE, data management, a Quarto report and version control. The case is the material for all of them. It is a field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, with a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. After a short opening on why reproducible tools matter, the morning takes the toolchain apart and gives you a first session in R on the emails of the case. In the afternoon you manage the data, from the file that the OAs published to the columns that an analysis needs, and the R work reaches its target. You reproduce one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose, put the result into a report whose numbers come from the code, and check that the report survives a clean run.

You leave able to find your way around an IDE, read a codebook and write the R of the tutorial, with one or two reanalyses that you reproduced from the public file and a report whose numbers come from the code that produced them. The day has no menu of specifications and sends nothing to a class chart, because the [one-day course on methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does both.

## How you work

The day is taught mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. Open it in a tab of its own and keep this page open beside it. Each part of the day has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step that you work at the keyboard has a button that opens the lab at the right task. This is the format in which the downloadable workspace, opened in an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), gives you most, because the IDE and the report have parts of their own. If you have not installed it, you follow those parts on the shared screen and do the R in the lab. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each part opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The class sends some of its answers in the chat at the same moment, so the day needs a facilitator.

## The parts of the day

- **[Before the day](before.qmd)** (about an hour, more with the installation). You read the case study and open the browser lab once, and you install R, an IDE and the workspace if you can, since this day uses them most.
- **[Part 1 – Credibility and the toolchain](part-1.qmd)** (ninety minutes). The part sets out the three Rs and the evidence on how often findings survive a check, then takes the toolchain layer by layer, from languages, editors, file formats and rendering to packages, version control, archives and licences, and ends with R running on your machine.
- **[Part 2 – R and the IDE](part-2.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You meet the paper of the case, the IDE, and R from the beginning on the emails of the case, and then you count and plot what came back.
- **[Part 3 – Data management and the reproduction](part-3.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after an hour for lunch). The part covers the public file and the course file, missing values, and raw and derived files, and then you reproduce one of the five reanalyses, and a second if there is time.
- **[Part 4 – The report and its record](part-4.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You look at a Quarto report from the inside, put your reproduction into the report with its numbers coming from the code, run it clean, and watch how a project keeps its versions.
- **[After the day](after.qmd)** (as long as you like). The page says where to go next.

[Start with Before the day](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
